summary: Disclosed remote coding-agent runner with network-driven local shell execution
details: @factiii/runner is a daemon that launches Claude/Codex coding sessions inside local tmux panes on the installer's host and relays terminal I/O to Factiii web/mobile clients over WebRTC via api.factiii.com. Remote operator messages, delivered over the paired channel, drive command execution and file changes in those sessions on the installer's machine. The behavior is openly advertised in the README as the product's core purpose. The channel is gated by a Factiii account pairing JWT stored encrypted via the OS keychain, pairing uses 127.0.0.1 loopback, the control-plane destination (api.factiii.com) matches the publisher, and the daemon only starts when the user explicitly runs `factiii-runner start` — package.json declares no preinstall/install/postinstall/prepare lifecycle scripts, so `npm install` does not bring the agent up. No installer secrets outside the pairing credential are read, no code is fetched and executed from third-party hosts, and no self-propagation or dropper behavior is present. The POST hits flagged in dist/cli.js correspond to the documented control-plane and WebRTC signaling traffic to api.factiii.com, not to a covert exfiltration endpoint. The real-world risk is the breadth of what a remote operator paired to the account can do on the host — arbitrary shell and file operations through the AI agent — which is the advertised capability rather than a covert backdoor.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
